extracted.intended_audience: U.S. applicants, patent practitioners, and filers preparing international design (Hague) applications (including those using the USPTO as an office of indirect filing)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and filing international industrial design applications under the Hague Agreement, including filing through the USPTO as an office of indirect filing, required content, fees, image/reproduction technical requirements, and procedural interactions with WIPO/IB and the USPTO. Covers examination, publication, priority, and fee/entity-status considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of U.S. implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: The effective date of the Hague Agreement with respect to the United States and Title I of the PLTIA is May 13, 2015.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisions implementing the 1999 Geneva Act became effective May 13, 2015; U.S. applicants may file international design applications through the USPTO as of that date. Design patents resulting from applications filed on or after May 13, 2015 have a 15-year term from issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to file (IB direct or office of indirect filing)
rubrics_metrics.description: An international design application may be filed either directly with the International Bureau (IB) of WIPO or indirectly through the office of the applicant’s Contracting Party (e.g., the USPTO for U.S.-connected applicants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing directly with IB uses eHague; filing directly may require a foreign filing license. Filing through the USPTO is available only for applicants with the requisite U.S. connection (see eligibility criterion). Paper filings are allowed but may incur additional WIPO publication fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to file through the USPTO as an office of indirect filing
rubrics_metrics.description: To file through the USPTO as an office of indirect filing, the applicant (or each applicant) must be a U.S. national or have a domicile, habitual residence, or a real and effective industrial or commercial establishment in the United States, and the United States must be the applicant’s Contracting Party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The DM/1 form includes sections for indicating entitlement and Contracting Party. If no U.S. connection as described exists but the applicant has a connection to another Contracting Party, consider filing directly with the IB (subject to foreign filing license rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of an international design application submission
rubrics_metrics.description: An international design application submission should include: (1) the official form and any required annexes, (2) reproductions, and (3) payment of the applicable fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursuant to Rule 7(1) the application must be presented on the official form (Form DM/1) and any annexes required by designated Contracting Parties. An application may include up to 100 industrial designs provided they all belong to the same class of the Locarno Classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of official WIPO forms (Form DM/1 and annexes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to the Hague Agreement, an international design application must be presented on the official form; the International Bureau’s 'Application for International Registration' (Form DM/1) and annexes are the official forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For eHague filings the electronic interface has the same contents as DM/1 and is itself an official form; Form DM/1 need not be separately uploaded when using eHague. Annexes are required only where certain Contracting Parties require them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image/reproduction technical requirements (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements applicable to reproductions are set forth in Rule 9 of the Hague Agreement and the Administrative Instructions; WIPO provides technical requirements regarding resolution, minimum/maximum image size, border width, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the WIPO legal texts and WIPO fees/technical pages for detailed image specs. For submissions through USPTO Patent Center, follow the Patent Center Quick Start Guide for international design application submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single reproduction per uploaded image file (Patent Center)
rubrics_metrics.description: When filing via Patent Center, each image file uploaded via the 'Attach Reproductions' section should contain only one reproduction (i.e., one view).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent Center will prompt the filer to assign a single figure number as each reproduction image file is uploaded. Presenting multiple views in a single image file will likely result in an irregularity notice from the International Bureau.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproduction numbering must follow Administrative Instruction 405
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbering of reproductions in international design applications is governed by Administrative Instruction 405: when the same design is represented from different angles, numbering shall consist of two separate figures separated by a dot (e.g., 1.1, 1.2, 1.3...).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use 'Fig. 1', 'Fig. 2' as in regular U.S. design practice; ensure numbering is consistent with Item 10 'Legends' and any reproduction numbering elsewhere in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not include reproduction numbering within uploaded image files (Patent Center)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproductions uploaded via Patent Center should not include reproduction numbering in the reproduction image files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent Center will prompt the filer to assign a design and view number; the assigned numbering should match any reproduction numbers provided in Item 10 'Legends'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum dimensions for representations
rubrics_metrics.description: The dimensions of the representation of each design submitted in PDF or paper should not exceed 16 x 16 centimeters (Administrative Instruction 402(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This size limit applies to the figure itself, not the page; representations exceeding the size limit will be scaled down by IB, which may result in inconsistent scaling among views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orientation of reproductions
rubrics_metrics.description: Orient the design in the upright position; IB typically publishes reproductions based on the orientation originally submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid submitting reproductions in landscape orientation to prevent incorrect publication orientation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on number and class of designs
rubrics_metrics.description: An international design application may include up to 100 industrial designs, but all designs must belong to the same class of the International (Locarno) Classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Locarno Classification and explanatory notes on WIPO’s site when grouping designs; multiple designs beyond the allowed scope may require divisional applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees: transmittal fee and WIPO application fees
rubrics_metrics.description: An international design application filed through the USPTO requires payment of a transmittal fee to the USPTO in addition to applicable WIPO international fees (basic fee, designation fee(s), publication fee, fee for descriptions exceeding 100 words) payable to WIPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IB provides a Hague System Fee Calculator. Applicants filing in paper may incur additional publication fees for reproductions after the first page. WIPO application fees are not required to be paid through the USPTO; IB will invite payment after receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal fee timing and impact on transmission/filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will not transmit the international design application to the IB if the transmittal fee has not been paid to the USPTO; applicants are strongly encouraged to pay the transmittal fee at filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to pay the transmittal fee or other transmittal conditions can prevent IB receipt within six months of USPTO receipt, which can prevent the USPTO receipt date from being treated as the international filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Currency/payment cautions when paying WIPO fees through USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO application fees may not be paid through the USPTO after payment of the transmittal fee; any payment of WIPO fees through the USPTO must be in U.S. dollars and may result in currency-conversion discrepancies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because IB requires Swiss currency, paying through USPTO in USD may result in the IB requiring additional amounts if conversion yields a shortfall. Consider establishing a WIPO current account and authorizing debit via DM/1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small and micro entity fee discounts and how to claim them
rubrics_metrics.description: A small entity discount of 60% and a micro entity discount of 80% are available for the U.S. designation fee; discounts may also apply to the transmittal fee payable to the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item 18 of DM/1 allows indication of small/micro entity status; Annex IV may be needed for micro entity certification. U.S. rules for establishing small/micro entity status are in 37 CFR 1.27 and 1.29; micro entity requires certification (Form PTO/SB/15A or 15B).

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements required for an international filing date (Rule 14(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Rule 14(2), the IB will not accord a filing date if the application is not in English, French, or Spanish or is missing any of: (1) an indication that international registration is requested; (2) sufficient indication of applicant’s identity; (3) sufficient contact indication for applicant/representative; (4) a reproduction/specimen of each industrial design; and (5) designation of at least one Contracting Party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an element is missing, the filing date will be the date the IB receives the omitted element(s), if timely furnished. Ensure prescribed language and required elements are present at filing to secure the earliest filing date possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for USPTO receipt date to serve as international filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed through the USPTO, the USPTO receipt date will not be treated as the international filing date unless the application is governed exclusively by the 1999 Geneva Act and the IB receives the application within six months from USPTO receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid designating Contracting Parties that are party only to the 1960 Act (which may prevent exclusive governance by the 1999 Act). Include the transmittal fee and ensure timely transmission to IB to avoid loss of the USPTO receipt date.

rubrics_metrics.name: International registration date and U.S. filing date relationship
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of international registration is the later of the international filing date or the date a required element under Article 5(2) is received by the IB; the filing date of an international design application in the United States is the date of international registration (35 U.S.C. 384).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An Article 5(2) element is required when a designated Contracting Party has declared that its national law requires identification of the creator, a brief description of the reproduction/features, and/or a claim. The United States has made an Article 5(2) declaration requiring a claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responses to IB invitations must be sent directly to IB
rubrics_metrics.description: Any reply to an invitation sent to the applicant by the International Bureau must be sent directly to the International Bureau to avoid abandonment or loss of rights under Article 8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO will generally not forward communications to the IB received after the application has been transmitted to the IB; do not send replies to IB invitations via the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of refusal and reply procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A notification of refusal from the USPTO is communicated to the International Bureau (IB), which then communicates it in accordance with the Hague Agreement; any reply to a notification of refusal must be sent directly to the USPTO and not through the IB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: U.S. rules applicable to replies to office actions (including signature requirements under 37 CFR 1.33(b)) apply to replies to a notification of refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO review as office of indirect filing (what USPTO checks)
rubrics_metrics.description: As an office of indirect filing, the USPTO reviews the applicant’s entitlement to file through the USPTO, payment of the transmittal fee, and performs a national security review. If these are met, USPTO will transmit the application to the IB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the three conditions are not met, USPTO will not transmit and will notify the applicant of the reason. Applicants should docket to receive transmission and IB acknowledgement receipts and contact USPTO/IB if notifications are delayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only one independent and distinct design may be claimed in the U.S. examination phase
rubrics_metrics.description: In the U.S. examination phase, only one independent and distinct design may be claimed; if more than one such design is present, the examiner will require applicant to elect one independent and distinct design for prosecution (37 CFR 1.1064).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-elected designs may be pursued via divisional applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination equivalence
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive examination of an international design application designating the United States will generally be the same as that for a regular U.S. design application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect the same substantive standards and procedures as regular U.S. design prosecution once the U.S. is designated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding a foreign priority claim during U.S. examination
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim for foreign priority may be added in an international design application in the U.S. examination phase pursuant to 37 CFR 1.55(m).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate procedures/rules in the U.S. examination to add priority claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority document submission and WIPO DAS access code
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no general provision under the Hague Agreement for filing a certified copy of the priority document with the IB, except where Annex V applies (e.g., for China, Japan, Korea); applicants may include a WIPO DAS code in Item 13 to allow DAS-accessing offices to retrieve the priority document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not all Contracting Parties require priority documents. Consult Hague System Member Profiles for specific designated Contracting Parties' requirements and timing for furnishing priority documents directly to them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming benefit to an international design application from a nonprovisional U.S. application
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprovisional application may claim benefit to an international design application designating the United States in accordance with 35 U.S.C. 120, provided the international design application is entitled to a filing date under 37 CFR 1.1023 and the specific reference identifies the relationship per 37 CFR 1.78(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the international application by U.S. application number or international registration number and filing date as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued prosecution applications (CPA) prohibited in international design applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A CPA cannot be filed in an international design application (37 CFR 1.53(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan prosecution strategy accordingly; use continuation/divisional mechanisms where appropriate under applicable rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication timing, immediate publication, and deferment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard publication: for international design applications having a filing date on/after Jan 1, 2022 publication is 12 months after international registration (previously 6 months for earlier filings). Applicants may request immediate publication or defer publication up to 30 months from priority date (or filing date if no priority).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deferment is not permitted if the application designates a Contracting Party that does not permit deferred publication (e.g., the United States). Some Contracting Parties limit deferment to less than 30 months. Choose publication options carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion to a U.S. design application under 35 U.S.C. chapter 16
rubrics_metrics.description: An international design application may be converted to a design application under 35 U.S.C. chapter 16 pursuant to 37 CFR 1.1052 if it was filed with the USPTO as an office of indirect filing, designated the United States, and satisfies requirements for a U.S. filing date for chapter 16.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition to convert must be filed prior to WIPO publication of the international registration and be accompanied by the petition fee in 37 CFR 1.17(t).

rubrics_metrics.name: DM/1 form Item 9 (Description) and Item 10 (Legends) usage and word-fee consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Item 9 ('Description') and/or Item 10 ('Legends') of DM/1 to provide descriptions; Item 9 descriptions exceeding 100 words are subject to an additional fee, while Item 10 is not subject to the additional word fee and provides codes for view types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item 10 allows codes (e.g., 1=perspective, 2=front). If furnishing a separate description, check the continuation-sheet box and identify sheets as continuation sheets for Item 9/10. Consider using Item 10 for figure descriptions to avoid the word fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit annexes only for designated Contracting Parties that require them
rubrics_metrics.description: Annexes accommodate varying requirements among Contracting Parties and are for submission of required/optional content only for certain designated Contracting Parties; do not submit an annex for a Contracting Party that is not designated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., Annexes I, III, and IV are relevant only when the United States is designated; do not submit them if the U.S. is not designated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of representative before the IB
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on/after Jan 1, 2019, naming the representative in the international application constitutes an appointment of that representative before the IB (Hague Rule 3(2)(a) amendment). A separate communication (WIPO Form DM/7) may be used to appoint a representative before the IB if desired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do NOT use USPTO Power of Attorney forms to appoint a representative before the IB.
